mechanism_narrative: A low and declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns during periods of low and declining UNRATE, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% indicates monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) combined with rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns despite rising HOUST and RSAFS, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity, which leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns during periods of rising INDPRO, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns during periods of rising PAYEMS, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% indicates rising inflation, which erodes corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) and increasing retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns despite rising HOUST and RSAFS, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the context of an economic recovery signals improving labor market conditions, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns during periods of declining UNRATE in a recovery regime, this hypothesis is rejected.
